laws.statement: A call with derived inputs returns without a panic.
A call with a cancelled context returns an error.
A call that fails returns the zero value of each value result.
A call that returns a false presence flag returns the zero value of each value result.
A read of an input that nothing stored returns the zero value.
Two calls with the same inputs on an unchanged subject return the same value.
A second call after a first call returns without a panic.

distinct-from.case: A subject that survives the first call and panics on the second.

laws.statement: A read of an input that nothing stored fails with the declared sentinel.
A second identical call succeeds after the first.
A read returns the value of the write before it.
A read observes every write that it causally follows.
A read of a client observes every write of the same client before it.
The writes of one client apply in the order in which the client issued them.
Two reads of one snapshot return the same value across a write between them.
One drain returns each element at most once.
Two drains of the same elements return them in the same order.
A drain gains exactly the elements that were written since the drain before it.

distinct-from.case: A drain that returns each written element and one element that nobody wrote.

laws.statement: A drain gains at least the elements that were written since the drain before it.
Each result is at least the result before it.
A read of a client never returns a version below a version that the client read before.
A write after a read has a version above the version that the read returned.
The output of a call does not contain the value that the directive declares unsafe.
A read returns the value that the directive declares unsafe exactly as the write stored it.

distinct-from.case: A store that returns derived values and changes the control characters of the unsafe value.

laws.statement: A call with the input at the edge of its declared domain succeeds.
A call with a value that its declared validator refuses fails.
A call with nil for an optional argument returns without a panic.
A call after the close fails with the declared sentinel.
A call before its declared predecessor fails with the declared sentinel.

distinct-from.case: A subject that refuses every call, before the predecessor and after it.

laws.statement: A call after its declared predecessor succeeds.
The named observation shows the effect of a call once the subject has settled.
A call returns before the clock passes its declared budget.
A count includes each occurrence inside its declared window and none outside it.
A registered task runs once the clock passes its instant, and not before.
A result changes once the clock has moved far enough.

distinct-from.case: A subject that reads the wall clock in place of the clock that it was given.

laws.statement: Two calls return the same value while the clock does not move.
A read of an entry fails with the declared sentinel once the clock passes the lifetime of the entry.
A read of a key after its delete fails with the declared sentinel.
A call changes the observation that the directive names.
Each call after the induced failure fails.
The verify of a value fails once the value has been tampered with.
A call inside an open transaction succeeds within the declared attempts.
A call succeeds within the declared attempts.
A call runs each hook that the registrar installed.
Each call changes the named observation again.
A read in one partition never returns the value of another partition.
The replay returns the entries in the order of their stamps.
An admitted append grows the replay by one entry.
An append returns a position above the position of the append before it.

distinct-from.case: An append that returns the same position twice.

laws.statement: The inverse returns the value that went into the forward call.
A write for a key that exists fails with the declared conflict.
An acquire of a held lease fails with the declared sentinel.
A write that carries a version that the cell has moved past fails with the declared mismatch.
A write of a value that the predicate rejects fails.
A call after the declared burst fails with the declared sentinel.
The leadership read reports no leadership after the resign.
A read finds nothing that a failed scope wrote.
A read finds nothing that a scope wrote before its commit failed.

distinct-from.case: A scope that rolls back a failed commit and keeps what a failed body wrote.

laws.statement: A call returns an error when a call of its dependency fails.
A reader finds no effect of a call that failed.

distinct-from.case: A writer that keeps nothing of a refused value and keeps a part of a write whose dependency failed.

laws.statement: After repeated failures of its operation, the callable refuses a call without calling the operation.
Calls with one value of the key go to one instance while it is healthy.
The callable releases each resource that it acquired, on every path of a failure.
The cache returns the value of its backing.
A second settlement of a transaction fails with the declared sentinel.
The put accepts the value that the get lent.
A read with the cursor of a page returns the page after it.
The compensation accepts the step that the call applied.
The reader finds no part of a write that the call refused.
A read after two writes for one key returns the value of the second write.

distinct-from.case: A store that accumulates the two writes under one key.

laws.statement: A second write for one key updates that key and adds no other.
The list of the variants contains each variant once, in the order of the declaration.
Each variant renders its declared text, and no two variants render one text.
Each variant is valid, and a value outside the variants is not.
The text of each variant parses back to the variant, and the text of no variant fails with the error of the parse function.
Each variant encodes its own text.
The text of each variant decodes to the variant, and the text of no variant fails to decode.
Each error value has a message that opens with the opening of the package and differs from the message of each other error value.
No error value of a package matches another error value of the package or of a package under no-overlap-with.
The message of an error type opens with the opening of the package and contains each member of text.
The hook Is of an error type agrees with the identity of the language on each error value of the package.
An error type with a cause returns the cause that it was given.
No value of an error type matches another error type of the package.
Combining two values in either order returns one value.
Combining three values in either grouping returns one value.
A batch read returns the stored value of each key, in the order of the keys.
The accessor of a fresh receiver reports no error.
The callable admits each position below the size of the collection and refuses the position equal to the size.
The callable returns what its sibling returns for one input.
The verify of a chain that appends alone produced reports no error.
An acquire after the release of a lease succeeds.
The stats of a pool change when the pool lends an object.
Each call of any sequence returns on the subject what it returns on the reference.
The use that the reader of the resource reads is between the lower and the upper bound after each call of any sequence.
Two replicas that any sequences of writes made diverge read the same state after a merge in either order.
Each state that the reader reads after a call is the state before the call or one of its successors in the graph.
Each call of the callable leaves the total of the quantity unchanged.
The rest of an iteration yields each value that a mutation wrote while it ran and no value that a delete removed while it ran.
Each message that an append recorded arrives on the channel of a subscription at least once.
Each published event arrives at least once, at most once or exactly once, as the delivery mode states.
Each event that a redelivery passed arrives once more than its publishes alone deliver.
A subscription returns each update that a trigger of its key caused after the watch started, in order, and no update after its stop.
A machine returns at most one reply to each inbound call.
On the stop event, a machine replies to each inbound call that it has not replied to.
From the stop event on, a machine returns replies alone.
A machine returns no effect after the step in which its error method returns an error.
Each effect that starts a call or a wait has a token that no earlier effect of its machine in the same epoch has.
Every history of concurrent calls has an order that keeps the real-time order of its calls and in which the reference returns the same results.
A read that runs beside other reads, without a write, returns what it returns with the same arguments when it runs alone.
Calls with one key that run at once share one computation of their result.
A write that returned success is readable after a crash.
Recovery after a crash during a write returns each record whole or not at all.
A read of a corrupted record fails with the declared error and returns no value.
A write that the medium cannot hold fails, and the state is as before the write.
A call that fails returns the value that the field of its request had before the call.

distinct-from.case: A read that returns the zero value beside an error for a request whose field is not the zero value.

laws.statement: Every history of concurrent transactions has a serial order of its committed transactions in which each read returns the same result.
Every history of concurrent transactions has no anomaly that snapshot isolation excludes, such as a dirty read or a lost update.

distinct-from.case: Two transactions that each read the key that the other writes and both commit, a write skew that snapshot isolation permits.
